mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising real interest rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the GDP decline is not followed by a market downturn.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or profit margins expand despite high unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO and a fall in HOUST over two months indicates supply chain inflation without corresponding demand growth, which erodes real earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.5% MoM and HOUST < -0.5% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong aggregate demand.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% during a period of negative GDP growth signals an emergency easing, which boosts risk appetite and triggers positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not observed outside recession periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in RSAFS above 5% signals robust household savings, which correlates with precautionary behavior and lower consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS and UNRATE above 4% for two months signals strong labor market absorption, which boosts consumer spending and supports earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 0.4% AND UNRATE > 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present outside recovery periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in HOUST exceeding 3% for four consecutive months signals a sharp drop in housing demand, which reduces construction and related sector earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not observed during other types of demand shocks.
